source_statement: File: openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/Milnes-rationality-conjecture-for-abelian-varieties-October-7-2026/build/sections/02_transport.tex (clone fd4aeeb2; no Lean entry for this manuscript in lean/formalization.yaml; manuscript not withdrawn per history.md; Oct-7 version note = citation update only). Proposition 2.1 [Transport] (lines 35-87), hypotheses verbatim: 'Let A/Qbar be an abelian variety of positive dimension with good reduction at w, and put V=H_1(A(C),Q). Suppose G subset GSp(V,psi) is connected reductive, its Hodge homomorphism h gives the Hodge structure of A, and its conjugacy class X makes this inclusion a Hodge embedding. Let gamma be a rational Hodge class of codimension r, represented on V by an alternating form satisfying (eq:transport-multiplier)' [xi(gv_1..gv_2r)=c(g)^r xi(v_1..v_2r), line 17]. Conclusion: 'there exist a positive integer n, an auxiliary good-reduction abelian variety B, a quasi-isogeny a:A_0^n->B_0, and a rational Hodge class kappa of codimension r on B such that, for the first-factor inclusion j:A_0->A_0^n, (aj)^*kappa_0=gamma_0 (2.2). The equality holds simultaneously in every l-adic realization with l != p and in the crystalline realization after extension to C_w.' Options: (1) B of CM type over Qbar (lines 62-63); (2) B over a finite K/K_0 realizing a prescribed weakly admissible filtration with finite local-field descent (lines 64-82). The normalization step is the paragraph 'A common rational normalization', lines 713-762: 'Tensor preservation of u_psi says that, in each realization, a^*theta_{B,0}=lambda_v theta_* (2.19), with a nonzero local scalar lambda_v. Let D=n dim A. Pairing with theta_*^{D-1} gives lambda_v = deg(a^*theta_{B,0} . theta_*^{D-1}) / deg(theta_*^D) =: lambda in Q^x (2.20). Both intersection numbers refer to rational divisor classes on the same abelian variety; their cycle-class traces are identical in every realization. The denominator is positive because theta_* is ample, and the numerator is nonzero by (2.19). Thus all the scalars in (2.19), including the crystalline one, are the single rational number lambda.' Then a^*eta_{B,0}=lambda^r f_0^*eta_{C,0} (2.21, lines 749-752) and kappa=(lambda^{-r}/[P:Q]) eta_B (line 758). Here theta_*=f_0^*theta_{C,0} in NS(A_0^n)(x)Q (line 723), u_psi=psi_W(x)psi_W^{-1}, u_eta=eta(x)(psi_W^{-1})^{(x)r} (lines 649-650). The quasi-isogeny a=b f_0 and its tensor preservation in every realization are IMPORTED from Kisin-Zhou 'Strongly compatible systems associated to semistable abelian varieties', arXiv:2505.02165v1 (KZ25b, a 2025 preprint: Thm 2.2.7 special-point theorem for option (1), lines 683-692; Thm 2.2.5/Prop 2.2.3 + Pappas-Rapoport 2024 Thm 4.10.6 + Gleason-Lim-Xu Cor 6.3 for option (2), lines 462-567). Main Thm 1.1 (00_intro.tex:29-56) is stated independent of the OAI CM-Hodge manuscript (00_intro.tex:111-112); only Cor 5.x 'algebraic-specialization' (05_reduction.tex:375-399) imports OpenAICMHodge2026 (revised Oct 6, not withdrawn). Grade: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated, not Lean-checked), with the key quasi-isogeny existence resting on a human 2025 arXiv preprint.
codex_claim_check: All of Codex's factual assertions check against the source. (a) 'normalizes local similitude factors by a ratio of rational intersection numbers of the same algebraic divisors': exact, lines 727-745; Codex's displayed formula matches (2.20) at lines 734-736 and its cited range 714-756 is the right passage. (b) 'does not create those maps': correct; the maps a=b f_0 come from imported Kisin-Zhou/Pappas-Rapoport integral-model theorems (lines 683-711), and the technique is applied only after a tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny of abelian varieties with good reduction exists. (c) 'compares realizations at one fixed reduction place': correct; 00_intro.tex:60-62 'The number q is common to all realizations for the fixed data; no comparison between different reduction places is required', and the figure caption 00_intro.tex:272-273 'There is no claimed map between the generic fibers'. (d) 'cycle classes of [P]-[O] vanish so it cannot replace heights/Kummer classes': this is Codex's own (correct) observation, not a manuscript statement; the manuscript transports classes in H^{2r} (Thm 1.1, gamma in H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), r>=0), never H^1 extension classes. (e) 'Do not cite as rationality of Q36 or a fixed 288 scalar': correct; Milne rationality concerns Tr(gamma_0 . c_1(D_1)...c_1(D_{d-r})) in Q, a pairing of a Hodge class with divisor products on a good reduction, not a period/L-value ratio or a mod-p tame coefficient. One imprecision in Codex's GLOBAL_CYCLE_SCOPE.md ('Two different kinds of independence'): it says the theorem 'supplies no assertion that those varying data [coefficient prime p and auxiliary prime ell] yield the SAME rational value'. Half of that is actually supplied: the theorem does give one value across ALL coefficient primes l != p plus crystalline at the fixed place. What is absent is independence of the reduction PLACE (the seed's auxiliary ell), and that absence is explicit in the source (00_intro.tex:60-62). Codex's conclusion (not a common scalar for the seed) stands, but the reason should be stated as place-dependence plus object-type mismatch, not coefficient-dependence.
what_it_would_need: The technique is: given an ACTUAL quasi-isogeny of abelian varieties a preserving a tensor whose GL-stabilizer is a similitude group (psi(x)psi^{-1}), the per-realization scalar lambda_v is forced rational by pairing against a complementary ALGEBRAIC class (theta_*^{D-1}) whose intersection numbers are realization-independent degrees. To become an input to any seed obligation it would need, for the tame identity C2(p,ell)=288(a_ell-2)R_(p,ell) / BD step C8 (the only lab target with a 'common scalar' shape): (T1) an actual algebraic morphism or correspondence between the object carrying C2 (the level-raised toric line Phi_ell/I in the component group of J_1=Pic^0(X_{N+,N-ell})) and E; but the lab's BD_CONSTRUCTION.md C8 records Hom(J_1,E)=0 (J_1 purely toric at ell_1, E good at ell_1), so the only comparison is the Galois-module isomorphism E[m] ~ V_J of BD05 Thm 5.17, defined only up to a unit, with no algebraic cycle to test it against; (T2) a realization-independent rational testing functional playing the role of deg(theta_*^D)>0; the seed's candidate is the regulator/Neron-Tate or p-adic height pairing R_(p,ell), which is not a rational degree, so the 'ratio of two integers' step has no analogue; (T3) cross-PLACE compatibility: the seed scalar must be the same for all admissible ell (and all p), whereas the theorem fixes one reduction place and C3_ASSEMBLY.md lines 140-150 records that no transition maps between the distinct Jacobians J_ell have been constructed; (T4) a transfer from even-degree cycle classes H^{2r} to H^1 Selmer/Kummer classes (not addressed anywhere in the manuscript). The precise missing theorem is C3_ASSEMBLY.md item 2: 'One rational number c has reduction C_m for every varying admissible pair and modulus, with one fixed normalization', i.e. a rational correspondence over a fixed number field between the varying level-raised Jacobians and E whose intersection numbers compute 288 without assuming #Sha=9 or Q36 (K-A). None of T1-T4 is supplied or reduced in cost by the source. For the other obligations: FIN uniform part, 59, 487, ORDER9 -- no Selmer or content statement at all; 2243, 4547, 5843 -- the proposition and Thm 1.1 require GOOD reduction at the comparison place (lines 37-38; 00_intro.tex:30-31), so the technique cannot even be instantiated with the seed's bad primes as reduction places; Q36 -- different rationality statement (cycle pairings vs. L''(E,1)/(2 Omega Reg)); plectic lemma TH at 5843 -- no theta-element or derivative content; cost reduction -- none (no computation is replaced).
obligation: None served. Nearest target it was proposed for: the fixed-scalar normalization in the tame identity C2(p,ell)=288(a_ell-2)R_(p,ell) / BD C8 ('matched scalar evaluation'), i.e. the cofinite route to FIN's uniform part. It supplies a comparison template only; it does not serve FIN, the named remainder 59/487/2243/4547/5843, ORDER9, Q36, lemma TH at 5843, or any cost reduction. K-A: the technique assumes no conjecture (fine) but outputs no arithmetic; K-RANK2: not applicable (no Selmer corank hypothesis, no Selmer output); K-GRADE: IMPORTED_PREPRINT, with the quasi-isogeny existence itself resting on arXiv:2505.02165v1.
new_observation: (1) Refinement of Codex's independence remark: coefficient-prime independence IS what the theorem delivers; what it explicitly does not deliver is reduction-place independence (00_intro.tex:60-62, 272-273). The seed's 288 must be independent of both the coefficient prime p and the auxiliary level/place ell, so the technique is structurally one axis short even before the object-type mismatch. (2) The structural reason the ratio trick cannot transfer is recorded in the lab's own C8 block: Hom(J_1,E)=0, so there is no algebraic map on which to evaluate an intersection ratio; the seed's 'local scalar' sits on a Galois-module isomorphism unique up to a unit, and the lab's index detector C9 avoids the unit for exactly that reason. (3) A closer template than the 1-dimensional ratio (2.20) is Lemma 1.2 'pairing-functorial' (01_preliminaries.tex:119-142): per-realization coefficients c_{i,v} are forced rational by solving one rational linear system against an invertible rational Gram matrix M_ij=deg(a_i b_j) via the projection formula. This is the multi-dimensional form of the technique and is the correct shape for a two-point (rank-two) comparison; but it needs a RATIONAL Gram matrix, which the Neron-Tate/p-adic regulator of P_1,P_2 is not. (4) Thin step in the source: lines 725-731 pass from preservation of u_psi=psi(x)psi^{-1} to a^*theta_{B,0}=lambda_v theta_* without stating the decomposable-tensor fact (Stab_GL(psi(x)psi^{-1})=GSp(psi), since u(x)v=u'(x)v' with all nonzero forces u'=lambda u, v'=lambda^{-1}v); elementary and correct, but unwritten. (5) The crystalline instance of (2.19) ('including the crystalline one', line 744) is not proved in the manuscript: it is the imported tensor-isogeny-class property of Kisin-Zhou 2025 (arXiv:2505.02165v1 §2.2.4, Thm 2.2.5/2.2.7), so the technique's novelty is only the elementary normalization; its substance is a 2025 preprint import. (6) Hypothesis Codex did not spell out: good reduction at the comparison place (Prop 2.1 line 37; Thm 1.1 00_intro.tex:30-31) excludes direct use at 2, 3, 2243, 4547, 5843 as reduction places. (7) Dependency hygiene: the Milne §2 technique does not depend on the withdrawn eightfolds/K3 papers (references.tex has no such entry; Markman 2026 is the human reference for Weil classes); the OAI CM-Hodge manuscript (revised, not withdrawn) enters only Cor 5.x, not Prop 2.1.
risks: Risk of over-reading: 'rationality' in the title invites conflation with Q36 rationality (q_E in Q with denominator <=174); the two are unrelated statements and the manuscript gives no period or L-value content. Risk of citing the §2 technique as if it were a theorem about the seed: it is a normalization identity valid only after a tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny of good-reduction abelian varieties exists, and that existence is an unrefereed import (KZ25b preprint) inside an unrefereed AI manuscript. Risk at the bad primes: any attempt to use the seed's remainder primes as the comparison place violates the good-reduction hypothesis outright. Risk of treating the pairing-functorial Gram-matrix lemma as a route to a rational regulator: the lab's regulator is real/p-adic, so inserting it would require assuming the conclusion (K-A). No lab endpoint (FIN, ORDER9, Q36) changes; no computation is authorized by this assessment.
